newsitem.title: UK: U.S. STOCKS IN LONDON MIXED, DRUG SHARES HIT.
newsitem.headline: U.S. STOCKS IN LONDON MIXED, DRUG SHARES HIT.

text.p: U.S. stocks traded in London were mixed on Tuesday, with drug company shares hit by a sector sell-off on Wall Street and Coca-Cola Co clawing back from its recent drop, traders said.
The Dow industrials, which gained 31 points to 8,062.11, were seen steady as bonds were higher and S&P futures slightly lower in GLOBEX trading.
By 1028 GMT, the September S&P contract was off 0.85 point at 941.70 and the long-bond futures were up 5/32 at 112-29/32.
"It's a mixed picture. It's still rotation," one trader said. "The drug stocks are looking weaker and were weaker in the States...the techs are fractionally firmer."
Volume was light due to traders taking summer vacations and the lack of corporate news, he said.
In London share activity, pharmaceutical companies headed lower in tandem with their sell-off overnight, blamed on a broker's comment on the sector.
Morgan Stanley reduced its recommended portfolio weighting of the drug sector based on a recent uptick in the group's selling, general and administrative expenses.
Merck and Co Inc shares fell 1/2 to $94-3/4 and Eli Lilly and Co lost 5/8 to $108-1/16.
On the positive side, Coke shares gained 1/4 to $62 in active trade, recovering slightly from its roughly seven percent drop the last two sessions to its close yesterday.
Technology shares were slightly higher with Intel Corp up 3/8 at $96-1/2, Texas Instruments Inc rising 5/16 to $122-5/8 and International Business Machines Corp unchanged at $103-1/8.
U.S. investors were expected to overlook a batch of economic data and wait for Wednesday's retail sales report for July.
On Tuesday, BTM-Schroders weekly chain store sales data are due at 1300 GMT and the Johnson Redbook at 1855 GMT. Second quarter productivity/unit labour costs data are due at 1230 GMT.
The Richmond and Atlanta Feds release regional economic activity for July at 1400 GMT.
